content.text:
If the current fill rate holds, only one device will run out of disk within a week: the ThinkPad X1 Carbon **8NM23J95R5I6** (emp-acme-1005), which is projected to be full in about 5 days [disk_trend/8NM23J95R5I6]. One other device, MacBook Pro **MT7PJB7N5LRE**, is already very low on space and is projected to fill up in about 10 days, so it will probably run out soon after the week ends [disk_trend/MT7PJB7N5LRE].

**Evidence**
- **8NM23J95R5I6 (ThinkPad X1 Carbon, emp-acme-1005):**
  - Free space fell from 176.8 GB to 26.5 GB over 30 snapshots, losing about 5.2 GB a day (slope −5.19 GB/day). Projected time to full: 5.1 days [disk_trend/8NM23J95R5I6, 8NM23J95R5I6/2026-05-14, 8NM23J95R5I6/2026-06-12].
  - It has 2.6% free (26.5 GB of 1024 GB), well below the 10% low-disk threshold [disk_low/8NM23J95R5I6, 8NM23J95R5I6/2026-06-12].
- **MT7PJB7N5LRE (MacBook Pro, emp-acme-1003):**
  - Free space fell from 36.8 GB to 10.2 GB over 30 snapshots, losing about 1.0 GB a day. Projected time to full: 10.2 days, so it falls just outside the 7-day window [disk_trend/MT7PJB7N5LRE, MT7PJB7N5LRE/2026-05-14, MT7PJB7N5LRE/2026-06-12].
  - It has 2.0% free (10.2 GB of 512 GB), also below the 10% threshold [disk_low/MT7PJB7N5LRE, MT7PJB7N5LRE/2026-06-12].
- No other device was flagged by the disk-trend or low-disk checks.

**Caveats**
- **Definitions:** "Run out of disk" here means the disk-trend check's estimate of when the disk will be 100% full. It uses a straight-line fit over the 30-day window and needs at least 7 data points; both devices had 30. "Low disk" means less than 10% free.
- **Projections:** These assume usage keeps growing at the same rate. A big download or a cleanup would change the dates.
- **No actions proposed:** This was a read-only question. If you want, I can propose disk cleanup for both devices, starting with 8NM23J95R5I6.
